sonnet.problem: The statement tests two claims at once: that the cry "Stop! Stop!" goes out, and that no one turns back.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The statement tests two claims at once: that knees knock, and that every face grows pale.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The card says the LORD tells Nineveh that He is against her. Nahum 2:13 only says "against you" and does not name who is being spoken to. Card 19 carries the same problem with "her chariots" and "her young lions", and card 20 with "her messengers".
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The joke contradicts itself. It says the apron has been clean "all its days" and then says everyone knows how long that lasts. It also does not match the image of a pool draining away, so it fails the same-action comparison.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
